status: research and architecture review only; no training, installation, Kaggle requests or submission
main_conclusion: Prior feature and retrieval ablations show a plateau; another small grid on the same representation is unlikely to yield a meaningful jump. Learned collaborative identity, qualifying-airing prediction, and temporal target alignment are genuinely different hypotheses. None supports promising 0.8.

evidence_review.weekly_retrieval: Frozen expansion changes top5 MAP +0.000308 main/-0.000159 later; retraining expanded pool degrades top5 on both windows. Merely enlarging weekly candidates is not promising.
evidence_review.regularity: All10 features improve main top5 by0.001406 but worsen later by0.001869. No robust improvement.
evidence_review.collaborative23: Existing added collaborative features are hand-designed user cosine and item cooccurrence. They improve main all80 by0.000789 over expanded19 but worsen later by0.003121. This is not a test of learned WARP embeddings or identity biases.
evidence_review.userCF: Standalone strict all80 main0.527310/later0.437792; useful signal exists but weak standalone ranking.
evidence_review.ALS_and_CBF: Early round ALS and CBF used different permissive180s labels; do not compare their reported MAP directly to strict80/top5 metrics. Root reports strict ALS weak as well; standalone quality does not prove absence of useful conditional latent features.
evidence_review.LightFM: No local LightFM training result found. Official documentation confirms WARP, learned user/item identity embeddings and biases; root independently verified participant used WARP-LightFM candidates/biases in two layers.
evidence_review.multiwindow: Previous pooled experiment used all80 HGB19 and two five-week snapshots. Recent retained groups fell3089/4813 versus4266/4721 early; filtered pooled laterMAP0.486095 vs filtered early0.491881. It did not test horizon-matched top5 LambdaRank24.
evidence_review.missing_truth_diagnostic_from_validation: Missing top5 outside old shortlist: main1363, of which1146 globally observed and217 globally unseen; later1410, of which1270 globally observed and140 unseen. User previously seen only0/12. This favors cross-user discovery of known items over purely global cold-item remedies.
evidence_review.participant_source_limits: Participant account is not the official target specification. Root verified reported public0.44203/private0.42905; this is no evidence for0.8. Top-five output does not prove ground truth is truncated to five. Winner notebook contents remain unresolved in saved source audit.

ap_mass_diagnostic_from_validation_agent.interpretation: Seen ranking and user-new globally-known discovery have comparable unrealized AP mass; not purely cold-start. Prior expansion improved oracle yet actual scoring failed, so retrieval alone cannot justify another candidate.

ranked_ideas.idea: Learned collaborative identity with a fixed reranking ablation
ranked_ideas.mechanism: WARP-LightFM estimates preferences shared across users and individual item biases. Current generic counts/context vectors omit explicit learned identity. Most missed truth items are globally known but user-new, precisely where learned collaborative factors may help.
minimal_test: After separate approval and user-managed installation if needed, fit one identity-only WARP configuration:16 dimensions,10 epochs,max_sampled10,fixed seed, historical>30% matrix for each cutoff. No metadata required initially.

Append score,item bias,user bias,and user/item embedding norms to unchanged v3 candidate rows; run one otherwise identical top5 ranker. Do not concatenate raw factor coordinates from independently fitted windows because rotation/sign axes are not identifiable across fits.

Only if conditional features improve robustly, inspect top30 WARP retrieval and seen/new slices; test expanded retrieval as a separate ablation. User bias is constant within a query, so direct ranking gain must come from item bias/dot product or tree interactions.
ranked_ideas.budget_estimate: 3 bounded small factor fits plus1 existing ranker; initially10 CPU minutes,2GB cap; single-thread CPU is acceptable. Exact runtime unknown before installed library pilot; stop rather than extend grid.
ranked_ideas.failure_criteria: No meaningful >=0.01 absolute top5 MAP gain on a declared primary window with no material reversal on later window, or no gain for user-new globally-known items. Standalone WARP need not beat v3; conditional feature ablation is decisive. Small0.001 changes do not justify Kaggle use.
ranked_ideas.risks: WARP optimizes implicit positive rankings rather than12-week counts. Unseen items have untrained factors and need existing fallback/context; never rank random cold embeddings. Fit each snapshot solely from its historical interactions.
ranked_ideas.evidence_status: Missing local experiment; supported by participant architecture as reported by root and official model semantics, not a guaranteed transfer.

ranked_ideas.idea: Predict qualifying uninterrupted airings, then aggregate expected counts
ranked_ideas.mechanism: Current weekly features estimate capped viewing seconds, whereas the hypothesized target requires>80% of one airing in one session and may rank frequent programmes. Equal expected minutes can correspond to radically different qualifying counts. A3600s cap further suppresses length dependence.
minimal_test: First perform a no-fit audit: qualifying-event rate by programme duration, user session-length quantiles, channel/weekly slot; quantify whether survival differences remain after existing scores.

Build one smoothed empirical probability table for a historical user/channel/weekly slot being watched and for session residual length exceeding0.8*airing duration, with backoff to channel/global statistics.

Integrate this probability for each known future airing, sum expected qualifying counts per item, and add one or two features to fixed v3 candidates. Retain separate max/any-view probability only if target interpretation requires it.
ranked_ideas.budget_estimate: One bounded streaming raw-session pass plus schedule aggregation,5 minutes preprocessing/2GB; at most one approved existing ranker fit thereafter. Avoid materializing user-by-airing cross product; restrict slots/candidates or sparse aggregates.
ranked_ideas.failure_criteria: No strong residual duration/survival structure in audit, poorly calibrated completion by duration on early held-out periods, or no robust >=0.01 top5MAP gain. Do not expand into neural survival modeling without evidence.
ranked_ideas.risks: Airing watches are dependent; summed probabilities estimate counts but1-product(1-p) independence is not justified. Need raw session identity or deterministic original rows, not reconstructed longest fragments across artificial splits. Future schedule is permitted; future viewing is never a feature.
ranked_ideas.evidence_status: Fundamentally different target representation; previous weekly minutes and per-item completion-share features did not test per-airing uninterrupted survival.

ranked_ideas.idea: Match temporal target horizon and ranking target before another architecture
ranked_ideas.mechanism: Current supervised fitting labels cover3–5weeks while submission spans12weeks. Persistent repeat programmes, seasonality and one-off films can change rank with horizon. Previous pooled HGB result does not resolve this mismatch.
minimal_test: No-fit diagnostic first: compare user top5 frequency-label stability as horizons extend from5 to8weeks; separate active-user cohort attrition from programme-rank changes.

One controlled top5 LambdaRank24 comparison with history throughApr13 and eight-week labels throughJun8, then freeze and evaluateJun8–Jul27 seven-week window. Compare to a short-label model on the same outer protocol, not to old-window raw scores.
If worth pursuing, refit the chosen specification using more recent actual history for final forecast, but report the unresolved12-week extrapolation explicitly.
ranked_ideas.budget_estimate: One or two extra temporal feature windows and two ranker fits,10–15 CPU minutes/2GB after approval; no broad date grid.
ranked_ideas.failure_criteria: Horizon extension barely changes top5 labels, or matched outer comparison fails robustly. Reject claims of an independent12-week validation:20weeks of logs cannot support long train history plus12-week fitting labels plus another12-week holdout.
ranked_ideas.risks: Longer labels also change recency/season and user activity. Mar23–Jun15 twelve-week fitting leaves only two weeks of history and six weeks validation, a severe covariate shift. Any existing model trained throughMay18 leaks into an outer May4–Jul27 forecast.
ranked_ideas.evidence_status: Unresolved hypothesis; validation agent confirms data geometry limits, requirements agent notes prior pooled test was a different model/objective.

deprioritized.pretrained_sequence_model: SASRec predicts next items; no established pretrained mapping to these programme IDs or12-week count target. Data/model installation and fine-tuning cost exceeds evidence. Consider only if sequence order diagnostics show residual gain over simpler seasonal/count models.
deprioritized.household_segmentation: Only behavioral clusters (channel breadth, time-pattern stability) are observable. Household identity or demographics are not. Hard clustering can shrink training samples; prefer conditional model interactions before separate cluster models.
deprioritized.title_alias_semantic_merging: Potentially useful if audit proves multiple IDs for equivalent programmes, but future metadata use is restricted. No merging based on guessed identity; preserve original submission IDs. Existing generic CBF failure does not prove semantic attributes useless, yet no evidence justifies costly embeddings first.
deprioritized.more_shallow_fusion_weights: Extensive saved ablations show tiny mixed gains, not the requested meaningful jump.

team_debate.research_priority: WARP representation first because it adds missing learned identity and targets globally-known user-new signal; keep fixed-pool feature test before expansion.
team_debate.requirements_priority: Temporal two-fit diagnostic first: no new dependency, observed history/horizon mismatch, prior failed pooling used a different model/target. Agrees WARP remains plausible but needs conditional evidence.
team_debate.validation_constraint: Neither long-horizon independent testing nor retrieval-only improvement is established. Twenty-week data geometry and overlapping prior holdouts limit confidence.
team_debate.resolution: Present both priorities honestly; root/user should choose a bounded next experiment. No experiment is authorized or run by this memo.

recommended_execution_order.phase0: No-fit temporal diagnostic first: quantify5→8week top5-label stability, active cohort shift, and seen/new AP-mass gaps. Estimated<=2min/<1GB using existing caches; do not reinterpret as clean independent12week validation.
recommended_execution_order.primary: One WARP-LightFM learned collaborative feature ablation on fixed v3 candidates, conditional on user approval and user-managed dependency installation. Captures both seen-ranking and user-new/global-known gaps; globallycoldsemantic machinery is not priority.
recommended_execution_order.primary_budget: At most3 historical snapshot factor fits, each16 dimensions/10epochs/max_sampled10/oneCPUthread/fixedseed, plus1 unchanged v3 ranker. Hardstop10min2GB for entire pilot, no tuning or submission. Actual runtime is an estimate until pilot.
recommended_execution_order.primary_features: dot-product score, item bias, user bias, factor norms; do not concatenate unaligned factor coordinates across snapshots. Identity-only first; no futuremetadata.
recommended_execution_order.fallback_if_dependency_unavailable: EASE fixed-regularization item-affinity features may reuse NumPy/SciPy, but requires separately approved dense Gram solve memory/time estimate; do not silently replace WARP or treat a linear model as equivalent.
recommended_execution_order.deferred: Per-airing survival forecast only if residual audit supports it; pretrainedLLM/sequence and broadgrids deferred.
recommended_execution_order.go_no_go: Look for>=.01 absolute top5MAP improvement on predeclared primary with no material later reversal plus actual seen/newcredit gains. Candidateoracle alone and negligible mixed gains are not sufficient for a scarce Kaggle submission.
